lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Supervised application: routine care, prevention, and sleep

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic routine care, prevention, and sleep task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: With a guardian, the learner has a conversation covering three routine-care categories -- roughly how consistent the learner's sleep schedule is, which preventive check-ins (such as dental, vision, or a general check-up) are due or coming up, and what reminders exist for anything that needs renewing on a schedule -- then the two agree on one realistic change to try for the next month.
safetyNotes: This lesson does not require writing down any real health condition, medication name, or medical detail -- only routine/habit categories and the one change agreed on.
The guardian conversation and the resulting plan happen entirely within the household; no outside professional needs to be contacted for this lesson.

simulationAlternative.description: If a guardian conversation cannot happen right now, the learner instead reads a provided fictional household's routine-care summary (a sleep pattern, one overdue preventive check-in, one recurring reminder) and writes the one realistic change that household should try next, using only the details given.

materials: adult-or-local: a few minutes of a guardian's time

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l04-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l04-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l04-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l04-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Why do you think routine and preventive care is often the first thing to slip when life gets busy, and what does that suggest about how you should treat it going forward?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u03-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Coverage of routine-care categories: Conversation covered all three categories (sleep, preventive check-ins, renewal reminders) at a general level. | Specificity and checkability of the agreed change: Change names a specific action and frequency. | Reasoning about why routine care slips: Names a specific reason routine care, versus urgent problems, tends to get deprioritized. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner and guardian set a specific date, roughly one month out, to check back on whether the agreed change stuck, and write what they'll do differently if it didn't.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic routine care, prevention, and sleep task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

resources.title: routine care, prevention, and sleep coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: With a guardian, the learner has a conversation covering three routine-care categories -- roughly how consistent the learner's sleep schedule is, which preventive check-ins (such as dental, vision, or a general check-up) are due or coming up, and what reminders exist for anything that needs renewing on a schedule -- then the two agree on one realistic change to try for the next month.
Coach direction: Before the conversation, think about which routine-care category you're least consistent about.

Learner prompt: Which of these do you think you're least consistent about: keeping a steady sleep schedule, preventive check-ins (dental/vision/general), or renewal reminders (like refilling or renewing something on a schedule)? Why do you think that one is hardest?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: routine care, prevention, and sleep complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Have the conversation with a guardian, covering all three routine-care categories.
Response 1 (t2-p1): We discussed my current sleep schedule in general terms (roughly how much and how consistently, not exact nightly detail).
Response 2 (t2-p2): We discussed which preventive check-ins are due, coming up, or overdue.
Response 3 (t2-p3): We discussed what reminders exist, or should exist, for anything that needs renewing on a schedule.

Equal-access rule: If a guardian conversation cannot happen right now, the learner instead reads a provided fictional household's routine-care summary (a sleep pattern, one overdue preventive check-in, one recurring reminder) and writes the one realistic change that household should try next, using only the details given.

resources.title: routine care, prevention, and sleep minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Why do you think routine and preventive care is often the first thing to slip when life gets busy, and what does that suggest about how you should treat it going forward?

Success checks: Coverage of routine-care categories: Conversation covered all three categories (sleep, preventive check-ins, renewal reminders) at a general level. | Specificity and checkability of the agreed change: Change names a specific action and frequency. | Reasoning about why routine care slips: Names a specific reason routine care, versus urgent problems, tends to get deprioritized.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: routine care, prevention, and sleep supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u03-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional routine care, prevention, and sleep condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Coverage of routine-care categories: Conversation covered all three categories (sleep, preventive check-ins, renewal reminders) at a general level. | Specificity and checkability of the agreed change: Change names a specific action and frequency. | Reasoning about why routine care slips: Names a specific reason routine care, versus urgent problems, tends to get deprioritized..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
